newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher on CPI optimism.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher on CPI optimism.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds led another day of broad gains for bonds, as the market looked forward to relatively low inflation in December and next year, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.12 to 170.21
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.12 to 171.16
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.14 pct to 167.21
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.20 pct to 171.37.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 161.5
Volume was moderate at 142 million shekels with most activity concentrated in unlinked bonds.
"The mood in the bond market is very positive and the market continues to rise. The whole market is rising and there are almost no sellers," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

He said unlinked bonds were leading the market due to expectations that inflation will fall to around 10 percent in 1997 from an expected 11 percent this year. "With yields of more than 15 percent the unlinked bonds are very attractive," he said.
Traders said, however, that Makams rose only moderately on low volume of 37 million shekels.
Dealers said low inflation would force the Bank of Israel to cut the short-term base interest rate, which is now 15.2 percent.

"The Bank of Israel will have to lower the rate because the inflation is falling," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel. "The market is waiting for a relatively low December consumer price index of 0.5 percent."

Traders said investors expected the central bank to cut its key lending rate following the parliamentary approval of the 1997 budget, which contains spending cuts of up to seven billion shekels. Parliament has until December 31 to approve the package.

"CPI-linked bonds also rose but activity was mixed," said the Leumi trader. "The main reason for the rise was that there are not enough sellers in the market. These bonds are becoming more attractive because the yield on unlinked bonds keeps falling."
Dollar-linked bonds rose following the sharp rise of the dollar against the shekel on Monday. The dollar representative rate was fixed on Monday at 3.273, compared with 3.253 Friday.
"Today's rise does not reflect the full rise of the dollar, and the bonds will continue gaining on Tuesday," the Leumi trader said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.27 shekels)
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
